title: Judge Suspends Poland's Constitutional Court Chief; Nawrocki Calls It a Takeover
dek: A judge elected by Tusk's majority suspended the tribunal's PiS-era president for a month. Police guard the court; Nawrocki flew home and calls it a forcible takeover.
body: The court's X account says its president is still in office. A judges' assembly is called for 3 November.

panels.label: Nawrocki and PiS Say
panels.text: Nawrocki calls it a “forcible takeover of a constitutional organ of the state”; the suspended president calls it a coup.

panels.label: Tusk and the Minister Say
panels.text: Tusk says restoring the rule of law “requires decisive action”; the justice minister says a lawfully elected judge acted without the government.

panels.label: The Stakes
panels.text: One side speaks of a coup, the other of the rule of law; beneath both is who holds the court that can strike down Poland's laws.
